criteria.text: States that English law has no general duty of good faith in commercial contracts.
Explains that a duty may be implied in relational contracts (e.g. Yam Seng, Bates v Post Office).
Notes that parties can expressly agree a good faith obligation and courts will give it effect.
Notes the implied term that contractual discretions be exercised rationally (Braganza).
Opens with a short 'Bottom line' / executive summary stating the overall conclusion and the most important risks before the detailed analysis.
Includes an 'Assumptions and open questions' section listing information that is missing or should be confirmed with the client.
